table.name: employee
table.purpose: One row per employee, identified by Employee_ID, with name, age, and city/team. Names are those of well-known English rugby union players and the City values are English rugby clubs (Bath, Bristol, Leicester, Sale, Wasps), suggesting a sports/rugby-themed sample dataset. Referenced by hiring (one-to-one) and evaluation (many evaluations per employee).

City.name: City
City.description: City or location associated with the employee. Values are English rugby club names (Bath, Bristol, Leicester, Sale, Wasps) rather than generic cities, and the related hiring table records a shop assignment per employee, so this may instead denote the employee's team/club or a branch/shop location named after a club. The exact meaning (city vs. team/branch) remains ambiguous.

Employee_ID.name: Employee_ID
Employee_ID.description: Primary key; unique employee identifier (1-10). Referenced by hiring.Employee_ID (one-to-one) and evaluation.Employee_ID (many-to-one).

Name.name: Name
Name.description: Employee's full name (first and last). All values are names of English rugby union players, consistent with a rugby-themed sample dataset.

table.name: evaluation
table.purpose: Records annual bonus awards given to employees, one row per employee per award year, linking to the employee table via Employee_ID.

Bonus.name: Bonus amount
Bonus.description: Monetary bonus awarded to the employee in the given year. Values range 2900-4000, likely in the local currency units (e.g., pounds/dollars).

Employee_ID.name: Employee ID
Employee_ID.description: Identifier of the employee who received the bonus; references employee.Employee_ID (many-to-one). Same employee can appear in multiple years.

Year_awarded.name: Year awarded
Year_awarded.description: Calendar year in which the bonus was awarded (2011-2018).

table.name: hiring
table.purpose: Records each employee's shop assignment: which shop they were hired into, whether the position is full-time, and the year they started. One row per employee (one_to_one with employee).

Employee_ID.name: Employee ID
Employee_ID.description: Identifier of the employee; references employee.Employee_ID (one_to_one, so each employee appears at most once).

Is_full_time.name: Is full time
Is_full_time.description: Whether the employee's position is full-time; stored as 'T'/'F' (true/false).

Shop_ID.name: Shop ID
Shop_ID.description: Identifier of the shop the employee was hired into; references shop.Shop_ID (many_to_one).

Start_from.name: Start year
Start_from.description: Year the employee started working at the shop (stored as a 4-digit string, values 2003–2013). Only the year is recorded; exact start date is not available.

table.name: shop
table.purpose: Despite the table name 'shop', the data clearly describes Finnish football clubs (Veikkausliiga teams): each row is a club with its home stadium, city, and head coach. The 'shop' naming appears to be a mislabeled or disguised schema; the table is referenced by 'hiring' via Shop_ID, which likely links clubs to coaches/employees.

District.name: home_stadium
District.description: Name of the club's home stadium/venue (e.g. Finnair Stadium for HJK, Veritas Stadion for FC Inter). All values are Finnish football venues, not administrative districts.

Location.name: city
Location.description: Finnish city where the club is based (Helsinki, Espoo, Turku, Lahti, etc.).

Manager_name.name: head_coach
Manager_name.description: Full name of the club's head coach/manager (e.g. Antti Muurinen at HJK, Job Dragtsma at FC Inter).

Name.name: club_name
Name.description: Name of the football club (HJK, FC Honka, FC Inter, KuPS, IFK Mariehamn, etc.) — Finnish top-flight clubs.

Shop_ID.name: club_id
Shop_ID.description: Primary key, values 1–9, one per club. Referenced by hiring.Shop_ID, so it identifies the club in the hiring table (likely coach hiring records).
